sentences.text:
Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.348 of 2024, under Sections 363, 376 I.P.C. and 3/4(2)
POCSO Act, Police Station South, District Firozabad, during the pendency of trial.
5. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have enticed away the victim from her house.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The FIR is delayed as there is no date and time of offence mentioned in it.
It is a clear-cut case of false implication as the victim has not whispered a single word against the applicant in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 02.07.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
7. LearnedState Law Officerhas vehemently opposed the bail application.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, taking into consideration the fact that there is no date and time of offence mentioned in the FIR and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant-Pushpendra Kumar, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence during trial.
(ii) The applicant shall not pressurise/intimidate with the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the date fixed.
10. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

11. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

Order Date :- 29.5.2025 (Ravi Kant) (Justice Krishan Pahal)
